themes.text: N-able restores hosted N-central after a hotfix, Microsoft patches an exploited Outlook zero-day, attackers hijack Xen Orchestra servers, and Fortinet fixes a critical FortiClient flaw.
Kraft Heinz sells Maxwell House for $650 million, Dutch Bros keeps growing fast, and El Niño trims Costa Rica's harvest.
The TotalEnergies team reportedly finds a sponsor to survive, Garmin may share rider locations with Waze, and Roglič is still without a 2027 team.
An Amadeus breach exposes airline passengers' data, JetBlue's first adults-only flights sell out, Hilton's Curio brand arrives on Kauai, and November deals are live.

desks.title: Technology
desks.blurb: The most important moves in AI, security and the infrastructure that runs it, with the original reporting linked.

items.head: Claude Code's 'don't ask again' file leaked secrets into public repos
items.text: Apiiro found 1,379 secrets, including database passwords and AWS keys, in .claude/settings.local.json files across public GitHub repositories. Rotate anything typed into approved commands and add the file to .gitignore.

items.head: OpenAI launches GPT-6 Cyber after its AI found 81 Firefox flaws
items.text: The security model, rated 'Critical' in cybersecurity under OpenAI's own framework, goes first to select Daybreak Red customers via API and Codex. OpenAI credits it with 948 Linux exploits and 81 high-severity Firefox bugs.

items.head: Researchers: malicious browser extensions could abuse Claude Dispatch
items.text: Forever Security showed an extension running scripts on claude.ai could send Claude Desktop tasks through Dispatch, launching an app in a test. Anthropic says Dispatch is being retired; turn it off if you don't need it.

items.head: Google warns LLMjacking can run up $1 million in stolen AI charges
items.text: Attackers use stolen cloud keys and tokens to run large language models on victims' accounts. Google says single incidents topped $100,000 in a day, and cumulative charges hit $1 million at some organizations.

items.head: N-able brings hosted N-central back after an emergency hotfix
items.text: Per Cyber Press, N-able upgraded every hosted N-central server to 2026.4 HF2 (build 2026.4.1.26), fixing seven CVEs, and finished early Nov 11. Self-hosted servers should stay offline until upgraded; N-able reports scanning tied to the public exploit code.

items.head: Microsoft fixes exploited Outlook zero-day in 1,093-CVE Patch Tuesday
items.text: Microsoft's November update fixes 1,093 CVEs, 63 of them critical. CVE-2026-124194, an Outlook spoofing flaw exploited as a zero-day, can leak a target's NTLMv2 hash when they open a crafted Office file. A researcher using Claude found it.

items.head: Attackers exploit Xen Orchestra auth bypass to take over virtualization hosts
items.text: Vates confirmed attacks on an authentication bypass (VSA-2026-062): a crafted cookie grants admin rights and can lead to root on XCP-ng hosts. Update to Xen Orchestra 6.9.1 or 6.10.0 and keep it off the internet.

items.head: Fortinet fixes critical FortiClient flaw malicious websites could abuse
items.text: CVE-2026-121529 (CVSS 9.1), dubbed Fortinet2Shell, lets a malicious website run code on FortiClient for Windows and Mac 7.2 and 7.4 through a local API. It isn't known to be exploited. Update to 7.4.8 or 7.2.15; there's no workaround.

items.head: GhostAction variant hits tens of thousands of GitHub repos with credential stealer
items.text: Socket found two accounts pushed a fake 'security-audit.yml' GitHub Actions workflow that steals credentials, now also searching files and full Git history for cloud and AI keys. Uber's athenadriver repo was among those hit.

items.head: Google patches Chrome zero-day exploited in the wild
items.text: CVE-2026-125350 is a use-after-free bug in Chrome's XML component, and Google says an exploit exists in the wild. Update to Chrome 157.0.8103.50 or later on Windows, Mac and Linux, and restart the browser.

items.head: Runware wants to mass-produce AI data center pods
items.text: The startup builds prefabricated, liquid-cooled pods in Romania and aims to bring them online within 48 hours of arrival, targeting 30MW of capacity a day by 2028. It claims $1 billion in committed interest.

items.head: Google eyes a 1,200MW data center campus near Richmond, Virginia
items.text: Google is doing due diligence on about 1,000 acres in Goochland County's West Creek. It hasn't bought the land; the site's tech zoning would allow a data center without a public hearing.

items.head: AWS eyes up to 15 more data center buildings in Missouri
items.text: AWS plans up to 15 new buildings on 890 acres near Danville in Montgomery County, separate from its $10 billion New Florence campus. It hasn't bought the land; construction could start 2027 to 2029 if approved.

items.head: A 444,400-square-foot data center is proposed for South San Jose
items.text: Menlo Equities applied to build on 15.5 acres beside Western Digital's campus. If approved, construction could start in late 2027, with operations by late 2029.

desks.title: Coffee
desks.blurb: What is moving the coffee business, and the shift from gas drum roasters to electric roasting.

sections.title: Industry and markets
sections.blurb: Prices, companies and rules that shape the cup.

items.head: Kraft Heinz sells Maxwell House and Gevalia for $650 million
items.text: Kraft Heinz agreed to sell its North American coffee business to One Rock Capital Partners for $650 million. It keeps a 30% non-controlling stake, and the deal is expected to close in mid-2027, Daily Coffee News reports.

items.head: Dutch Bros revenue jumps 29.8% as it reaches 1,273 shops
items.text: Dutch Bros posted third-quarter revenue of $549.8 million, up 29.8%, with net income of $37.2 million. It opened 48 shops in the quarter and is targeting about 250 openings in 2027.

items.head: Costa Rica trims harvest estimates by 10% to 15% on El Niño
items.text: Costa Rica's coffee institute ICAFE cut regional harvest estimates by 10% to 15% after irregular rain and heat disrupted fertilization and hurt the quality and weight of export coffee. These are cuts to earlier forecasts.

sections.title: Electric roasting watch
sections.blurb: Machines and experiments moving roasting off gas.

items.head: Sandia tests stored solar heat for drum roasters
items.text: Sandia National Laboratories and Albuquerque's Michael Thomas Coffee stored solar electricity as heat in a rock bed and fed it to a drum roaster, reaching 600°C. The goal is a bolt-on retrofit that cuts gas use.

items.head: Coffee Crafters ships the all-electric Duo
items.text: A compact fluid-bed roaster for 200 grams to 2 pounds a batch, up to 10 pounds an hour, on 240-volt power. It starts at $2,995.

items.head: Rex Roaster's 4-pound electric drum plugs into 120 volts
items.text: The manual, stainless machine runs on a standard 20-amp outlet, works with Artisan profiling software and lists at $6,000.

items.text: The National Coffee Association's annual convention comes to the JW Marriott Austin.

items.head: TotalEnergies team finds a three-year title sponsor to survive into 2027
items.text: The French team, which had about a week to find a sponsor before UCI 2027 registration, has reportedly secured three years of title funding, per Ouest France. It will get a new name and colours, with Pardus as bike sponsor.

items.head: Unconfirmed: Garmin may share riders' locations with Waze drivers
items.text: Code in Garmin Connect v5.31 hints at an opt-in 'Waze Location Sharing' feature that would use LiveTrack data to show drivers nearby cyclists. Neither Garmin nor Waze has announced it, and there's no timeline.

items.head: Roglič is the last big name without a 2027 contract
items.text: The 37-year-old reportedly turned down Lotto-Intermarché, and talks with Visma-Lease a Bike ended. He hasn't ruled out retiring; Pinarello-Q36.5, Unibet Rose Rockets and Tudor still have room.

items.text: Third annual fall ride with 38, 65 and 105-mile options starting at 7:30 AM from the Pineland YMCA.

items.head: Turkey Roll Bicycle Rally, Denton, Texas
items.text: A Saturday bicycle rally in Denton on November 21, listed on NWCC's 2026 calendar of Texas bike rides. Check the organizer for routes and registration.

items.head: Texas MS 150: Houston and Austin to College Station
items.text: Two-day ride with starts in Houston and Austin, an overnight in La Grange and the finish in College Station.

items.text: 21 stages and 3,479km, with time trials at Blois–Chambord and Toulouse and a Montmartre finale in Paris.

desks.title: Travel
desks.blurb: What affects your next trip, the rules and safety basics to check first, where to go, and offers worth a look.

items.head: Amadeus breach exposes data from at least five airlines' passengers
items.text: Unauthorized access to the airline booking provider ran from August 2023 to September 2026. Cathay Pacific, Japan Airlines, ANA, Korean Air and Condor are affected. Watch for phishing emails posing as your airline.

items.head: JetBlue and Virgin Voyages sell out their first adults-only flights
items.text: Their 'Do Not Disturb' package paired a Virgin Voyages cruise with JetBlue's first adults-only flights. All 60 cabins sold out within days; it's a one-time offer for now.

items.head: Hilton's Curio Collection opens its first Hawaii hotel on Kauai
items.text: The 210-room Hale Hokuala Kauai offers Pacific views, open-air spaces and preferred tee times for guests.

sections.title: Restrictions and entry rules
sections.blurb: Advisories, entry permits and health notices to check before you book.

items.head: Don't pay for ETIAS yet: Europe isn't taking applications
items.text: The EU says the permit is not operational and has no launch date. Over 150 look-alike sites charge €50 to €178; the official fee will be €20.

items.head: Americans need a UK ETA before flying to Britain
items.text: The electronic travel authorisation costs £20 on GOV.UK, covers visits of up to six months, and every traveler needs one, including children. Unofficial sites charge more.

items.head: CDC: reconsider travel to Ebola areas of eastern DR Congo
items.text: A Level 3 notice covers Ituri, North Kivu and South Kivu provinces. Level 2 precautions apply to the rest of DR Congo and Uganda.

items.head: Lonely Planet names its Best in Travel 2027
items.text: The 25 picks include Okinawa, Oman, Šibenik, Bariloche, Da Nang and Rabat, plus US choices Maryland, New Mexico and the Northern California redwood coast.

sections.title: Safety and smart-travel tips
sections.blurb: Simple habits that save money and trouble.

items.head: Enroll in STEP before any international trip
items.text: The State Department's free Smart Traveler program emails embassy alerts for your destination and helps the embassy reach you in an emergency.

items.head: Buy entry permits only on government sites
items.text: Look-alike sites charge several times the real fee for UK ETAs and EU permits. Skip sponsored search results and go to GOV.UK or the official EU site directly.

items.head: Get TSA PreCheck to keep shoes and laptop in place
items.text: Enrolled travelers keep shoes, belts, laptops and liquids in their bags at screening. Enrollment costs $77.95 to $85 depending on the provider.

items.head: Use Mobile Passport Control when flying home to DFW or Houston
items.text: US citizens can submit passport details and customs answers in a free app, then show a QR receipt to the CBP officer. Both DFW and IAH take part.

items.text: 3,000 points at resort and upscale hotels, 1,000 elsewhere, on cash or points stays. Register before your first stay.

items.text: Rises to 4,500 at resorts on cash stays of two nights or more, through November 22.

items.text: Use promo code 212109 on 4- to 27-day SUV or minivan rentals picked up by December 31 to get the fifth day free.
